title: UniGCRec: Unified User-Item Quantization for Generative Cross-Domain Recommendation

problem.claim: Cross-domain sequential recommendation seeks to improve target-domain prediction by leveraging interaction histories from multiple domains.

gap.claim: Existing approaches are unreliable under limited overlap and distribution shifts, while generative methods still face user-item asymmetry and difficulty selectively transferring relevant source-domain signals.

contributions.claim: UniGCRec constructs a cross-domain user profile and quantizes both users and items into CSC-IDs integrating semantic and collaborative signals.
It places user and item representations in a shared discrete CSC-ID space to support preference-aware selective transfer under low-overlap settings.
Its generator uses a user CSC-ID prefix and target-domain item CSC-ID history for next-item generation with trie-constrained decoding.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on public multi-domain benchmarks report consistent gains over strong baselines, with particularly strong gains on several target domains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cross-domain histories can improve target-domain recommendation.
Limited overlap, long-tail and unseen items, and distribution shifts weaken conventional approaches.
Generative approaches avoid raw ID alignment but retain user-item asymmetry and selective-transfer difficulties.
UniGCRec symmetrically quantizes users and items and conditions generation on CSC-ID representations with constrained decoding.
Benchmark experiments report gains over strong baselines.

source_observation.claim: Limited entity overlap and cross-domain distribution shifts can make shared-entity, co-occurrence, and atomic-ID representations unreliable.

interpretation.claim: Cross-domain transfer may benefit from representations that preserve semantic information while reducing dependence on exact ID overlap.

application.claim: For low-overlap recommendation settings, consider aligned discrete representations for users and items that combine semantic and collaborative signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the approach performs outside the reported public multi-domain benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, sizes, splits, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not quantify the reported gains or define the low-overlap conditions.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, ablations, or reproducibility information.
